doc.title: Howard Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019

title: Listening today, no limits on instruments, Roland Kirk
summary: He listens to WGBO; he argues instruments have no limits, never meant to innovate on tuba, and praises Roland Kirk's evolution.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Okay. What do you listen to now? Do you like to listen to music now?
Yeah I do. The newest stuff I hear is on WGBO. I haven’t gone much deeper into things. I almost never do KCR. They have interesting stuff.
You said KCR makes me think of Phil Schaap.
Yeah, is he there no longer?
I don’t know, I think he’s still there, but there’s a guy that nothing gets past him.

I had a chance to kind of get even with him because he kept pumping me about this idea of multiple instruments. And what you can get out of the instruments you play. And I insisted that there were no limitations to what you can get out of what instrument, it just hasn’t been discovered yet. And so he had this thing, it seemed like he was ready in advance, about how well there are limitations and you say it isn’t finished. But no one can say it until everything has been tried, he was kind of like, “What?” So I said well that hasn’t been my experience. My experience is that if a saxophone player wants to play like a trombone and slide like that, if that’s what it takes for him to express himself he’ll do it. She’ll do it. It’s like it’s just a matter of opportunity to do what you think you ought to do. I never said I’m going to innovate the tuba into modern jazz. I never thought like that. It’s just a sound I wanted to make. And it goes for the baritone sax too ‘cause nobody plays like me. © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-
You had your own sound for sure. And most of the people who innovate aren’t aware that it’s a conscious effort I think. That’s what makes it so terrific.

Even Roland Kirk, who you have to say put a little bit of thought into what he was going to do, I mean, you wouldn’t imagine playing three saxophones was a good idea just one day and decide to go and do it. It evolved. And he was an evolving cat too. He used to play baritone like Harry Carney. And flute. He turned into a great flute player at a time when flute was still new and everybody was getting one. His sound was so far ahead of everybody.
